title: From upstream PR to ODH images and a staged RHOAI installer
scope: Current ODH / next RHOAI development path. rhoai-3.6 is the inspected release-branch example; EA branch gates differ. Configuration evidence, not an audit of live Konflux resources or successful build runs. SDK package publication and contrib adapter builds are separate entry paths; provider configuration and image selection join the existing service/operator paths. SDK/contrib effective main rules observed; PyPI environment approvals and adapter release selection remain Q7–Q8.

nodes.title: SDK change → upstream PR
lines: eval-hub/eval-hub-sdk · models / client / adapter / CLI
nodes.detail: Start with an SDK PR. Client/CLI-only consumers can stop after installing the published package; adapter-facing changes require a separate adapter image rebuild. The EvalHub Go service image does not install this Python SDK.

nodes.title: S1 · SDK review and configured CI
lines: Effective main gate: PR + 1 approval; no required status checks
Unit Python 3.12–3.14, lint/type, pre-commit, commitlint, Trivy
nodes.detail: Effective main rules require a PR and one approving review, with no required_status_checks rule returned. Classic branch-protection API returned 404. CODEOWNERS, last-push approval and thread resolution are not required by the observed rules. CI configures unit tests on Python 3.12/3.13/3.14, Ruff, mypy, pre-commit, commitlint and a Trivy HIGH/CRITICAL failure step. E2E has continue-on-error: true. Review and resolve applicable CI before merging as a working practice; these jobs are not established as enforced merge checks.

nodes.title: S2 · Publish and verify the SDK package
lines: main push → TestPyPI dev build; published release → PyPI
SCM-derived version; OIDC environments; approval policy? Q7
nodes.detail: main pushes build a dev distribution for TestPyPI. A published GitHub release triggers a separate build and upload to PyPI in the pypi environment using OIDC. Version comes from setuptools_scm and Git history/tags. Select the release/tag containing the merged change and verify the intended wheel/sdist is installable from the intended index. Neither publish workflow depends on the Tests workflow. Environment reviewer and tag/release authorization rules were not audited; TestPyPI success alone is not production publication.

nodes.title: S3 · Update every affected SDK consumer
lines: Contrib PR: requirements + constraints / lock + adapter migration
Verify installed SDK version; publishing alone does not rebuild
nodes.detail: For adapter-facing changes, open a contrib PR for each affected adapter: update SDK requirements and any constraints/lock files together, migrate changed interfaces and exercise callbacks/results against the target service/sidecar. Inspect currently permits eval-hub-sdk[adapter]~=1.0.5 but its constraints pin eval-hub-sdk==1.0.5, and its Containerfile applies both. Regenerate constraints using the adapter README; do not assume a compatible range picks up a new release. Its unit workflow installs the SDK requirement without that constraints file, so verify the built image too. Direct SDK clients/CLI users instead install the published package and validate against their target service. No inspected workflow automatically opens consumer bump PRs or rebuilds adapters on SDK publication.

nodes.title: Contrib change → adapter PR
lines: eval-hub/eval-hub-contrib · direct change OR SDK consumer bump
nodes.detail: Direct adapter/framework/dependency/provider changes start here independently of an SDK release. Include main.py, Containerfile, requirements/constraints, tests and provider.yaml as applicable; new adapters also need the documented Makefile targets and README.

nodes.title: C1 · Contrib review and configured CI
lines: Effective main gate: 1 approval + squash; no required status checks
Path-specific tests; new-provider YAML; commitlint / security
nodes.detail: Effective main rules require a PR with one approval and allow squash merges only; no required_status_checks rule was returned, and classic branch-protection API returned 404. Run the applicable adapter-specific tests and inspect configured commitlint, CodeQL and Trivy jobs. Trivy has a HIGH/CRITICAL failure step. Provider validation runs for adapters/** PRs into main but its script only checks new adapter directories for provider.yaml existence and parseable YAML: it does not validate the full provider schema or existing directories. Test coverage is workflow/path-specific; a skipped job is not adapter validation.

nodes.title: C2 · Build and push the selected adapter images
lines: adapters/** push to main or v* branch; manual rebuild available
quay.io/evalhub/community-<adapter>:<SHA> + latest / branch
Verify push, digest, actual SDK and supported architecture
nodes.detail: After merge, build-images.yml detects changed adapters on main or v* branch pushes restricted to adapters/**; it is not a tag-push release trigger. It builds each selected Containerfile and pushes commit-SHA and channel tags (main → latest; otherwise branch name). A root-only/workflow-only change does not trigger this publisher, and SDK publication alone is not a contrib push. Manually dispatch with adapter input when change detection misses the needed rebuild; build-all-images.yml is a separate manual, explicit matrix, not dynamic discovery of every adapter. ToolEval expands to both adapter and toolbench-server images; clear maps to community-ibm-clear. RULER also has a separate publisher targeting the same tags. Quay credentials and a successful build/push are operational gates, but the publisher has no needs dependency on adapter tests or security jobs. The inspected workflow uses an Ubuntu docker build without an explicit multi-platform matrix. Verify digest, installed SDK/dependencies, architecture and runtime compatibility before selection.

nodes.title: P1 · Reconcile provider definitions when changed
lines: Contrib provider.yaml → EvalHub config/providers PR (G1)
Image check skips new providers on PRs; drift check is post-merge
Sync operator ConfigMaps; update image variables / resources
Then join service and operator source promotion paths
nodes.detail: If benchmark metadata, runtime fields or provider definitions change, reconcile the contrib provider.yaml into eval-hub/eval-hub config/providers/<id>.yaml in a separate PR and pass G1. The inspected contrib publisher does not copy provider definitions into EvalHub. EvalHub validates referenced images on matching PRs/pushes, but newly added providers are skipped on PRs and checked after merge. Its ConfigMap check runs on main pushes, nightly at 02:00 UTC and manual dispatch, not PRs; it detects drift against upstream TrustyAI and skips Kustomize image variables, so cannot prove the selected image digest. In a TrustyAI PR run hack/sync-evalhub-providers.sh <source-ref>, inspect generated ConfigMaps/kustomization and preserve intentional downstream overrides. For a new provider add the base Kustomize image variable and base/ODH/RHOAI params entries, then sync module manifests. Both service and operator PRs are conditional on the actual change.

nodes.title: P2 · Select adapter references and sync module manifests
lines: Operator params.env: base, ODH and RHOAI overlays
Inspect: base latest; ODH / RHOAI v0.6.12 (not latest)
Copy generated config into module manifests; operator PR → G2
RHOAI branch mapping / rebuild or mirror / policy? Q8
nodes.detail: For an adapter-only update, existing provider metadata may remain unchanged, but prove which reference and digest the deployment selects. TrustyAI base params uses community-inspect:latest while upstream ODH/RHOAI overlays and the inspected downstream rhoai-3.6 overlay select community-inspect:v0.6.12. A main/latest build does not update that pinned selection. Build the chosen release branch or deliberately change the selected reference in an operator PR; resolve and record its digest because channel/branch tags are mutable. Update affected params entries, run hack/sync-trustyai-module-manifests.sh to copy the config tree into trustyai-operator-module/config/manifests-template, review both trees, and pass G2 before G4/G6/G8 and G7/G9–G14 as applicable. The observed RHOAI overlay references a community adapter image, so do not assume a separate RHEL adapter rebuild/nudge. Confirm approved release/branch, platform/security eligibility and any mirror/rebuild/relatedImages mapping with maintainers (Q8).

nodes.title: EvalHub PR → upstream main
lines: eval-hub/eval-hub
nodes.detail: Start with a PR in the canonical EvalHub repo. All binaries are built into the same container; the API, init, sidecar and MCP binaries do not represent four independent image promotion chains.

nodes.title: TrustyAI operator PR → upstream main
lines: trustyai-explainability/trustyai-service-operator
nodes.detail: This repository contains both the workload operator and the TrustyAI module operator. Follow both artifacts into the installer.

nodes.title: G1 · Required upstream merge gate
lines: 1 approval + CODEOWNERS + latest-push approval
Required checks + resolved review threads; up-to-date branch
nodes.detail: Effective main rules require quality-checks, Gosec Security Scanner, gosec, dependency-review, CodeQL, docker-build-check; one review, code-owner review, last-push approval, stale-review dismissal and resolved threads. These are observed rules, not an audit of bypass actors. CI quality-checks runs formatting/vet, builds/tests including FVT, and documentation verification.

nodes.title: G2 · Upstream CI / merge policy ? Q2
lines: Controller + module smoke / manifest checks; Prow
Which checks and approvals are enforced remains open.
nodes.detail: GitHub workflows configure controller and module tests. Prow always runs images, and e2e runs for matching paths or an explicit test command. The enforcement layer was not established; do not infer that every listed workflow blocks merging.

nodes.title: G3 · Sync PR → ODH main
lines: opendatahub-io/eval-hub
Hourly at :23 UTC / manual; conflicts fail; PR merge required
nodes.detail: The hourly sync workflow uses a merge strategy, opens/updates a sync PR and fails on conflict. Effective main rules observed via GitHub require one approval. There is no workflow evidence that opening the sync PR automatically advances stable. Upstream CI also publishes quay.io/evalhub/evalhub independently.

nodes.title: G4 · Upstream sync PR → ODH main
lines: opendatahub-io/trustyai-service-operator
Pull bot PR: auto-approve / enable auto-merge; cadence ?
nodes.detail: The workflow recognizes pull[bot], approves the sync PR and enables merge-commit auto-merge. This confirms the PR handling, but not the Pull app source configuration or sync schedule. Effective ODH main rules include one approval and CODEOWNERS/latest-push approval.

nodes.title: G5 · ODH main → stable sync PR
lines: Push to main / manual creates sync PR
Gate: merge PR; resolve conflicts and destination requirements.
nodes.detail: Sync main to stable is a PR workflow with fail-on-conflict=true. It must merge before the stable push image build runs. Required checks on stable were not established.

nodes.title: G6 · ODH main → incubation → stable PRs
lines: main push opens incubation PR; incubation push opens stable PR
Module image has a separate main build (Q3).
nodes.detail: Two workflows open promotion PRs. Creating these PRs is not evidence they have merged. The module operator build currently targets main, while the workload operator stable definition targets stable.

nodes.title: ODH component image builds
lines: EvalHub stable → quay.io/opendatahub/odh-eval-hub
Workload stable + module main → opendatahub operator images
Tag: odh-stable; Konflux build / scan tasks (policy: Q4–Q5)
nodes.detail: Stable EvalHub and TrustyAI workload PipelineRuns resolve odh-konflux-central pipeline/multi-arch-container-build.yaml. Module PipelineRuns target main and publish odh-trustyai-module-operator:odh-stable. Central scan task presence does not prove all findings block selection. Community quay.io/evalhub/evalhub is a parallel upstream output, not the RHOAI container being promoted.

nodes.title: G7 · ODH → Red Hat source promotion ? Q1
lines: red-hat-data-services/{eval-hub, trustyai-service-operator}
Destination builds verified on rhoai-3.6
Source branch / sync bot / cadence / approvals: OPEN
nodes.detail: The destination release PipelineRuns are verified. The ODH → Red Hat component synchronization mechanism and intermediate branch sequence have not been established. Do not treat this edge as an automatic promotion of ODH images: Red Hat performs a separate build from downstream source.

nodes.title: G8 · Select manifests + immutable image digests
lines: Daily 06:00 UTC / manual manifest-update PR
Merge updated SHA / digest pins; eligibility policy ? Q4
nodes.detail: ODH Update Manifest SHAs runs make update-refs-shas and resolves image digests when updates are needed, opening a PR. Failed component fetches add do-not-merge and fail the workflow. manifests-config.yaml pins TrustyAI module manifests from ODH main and keeps explicit image digests. Build Config separately lists selected relatedImages. These configurations can lag independently; atomicity was not established.

nodes.title: G9 · Merge / backport into the release branch
lines: Branch-specific tests + approvals; freeze exceptions when enabled
EA gatekeeper configured for 3.6-ea.1 / 3.6-ea.2
nodes.detail: Push builds run after code reaches the release branch. The inspected main gatekeeper definition calls shared post-codefreeze logic for two EA branches; confirm its deployed status, required label/approval policy, and branch coverage. Do not assume the EA gate applies to every development branch.

nodes.title: ODH installer operator build
lines: opendatahub-io/opendatahub-operator main push
Output: opendatahub-operator:odh-stable; path filters apply
nodes.detail: The checked-in CI push pipeline builds Dockerfiles/rhoai.Dockerfile with BUILD_TYPE=CI via multi-arch-operator-build.yaml and nudges bundle/bundle-patch.yaml. A component image existing in Quay does not itself update this source build.

nodes.title: RHOAI component image builds
lines: Release-branch push → Konflux hermetic builds
EvalHub + workload + module → quay.io/rhoai/*-rhel9
Four architectures; scans / attestations policy ? Q5
nodes.detail: Verified release PipelineRuns build source/images from downstream Dockerfile.konflux definitions for x86_64, ppc64le, s390x and arm64. Each inspected component push pipeline sets build-nudge-files to build/operator-nudging.yaml. Image publication and policy approval are separate states.

nodes.title: ODH development bundle / catalog path
lines: ODH-Build-Config pins relatedImages; bundle build
Operator stable → bundle sync every 2h / manual
Bundle → catalog nudge; processor / policy details ? Q4–Q5
nodes.detail: The ODH bundle CI PipelineRun publishes opendatahub-operator-bundle:odh-stable and nudges catalog/catalog-patch.yaml. A bundle-patch-only change is excluded from the direct bundle build and needs processed output. Bundle Sync CI generates bundle content from opendatahub-operator stable. The complete active ODH processor/catalog policy was not audited; this is contextual to the requested ODH image endpoint.

nodes.title: G10 · Component digest nudge PR → installer
lines: rhods-operator build/operator-nudging.yaml
Bot + one-file + title/version feasibility → auto-merge path
nodes.detail: The installer insta-merge workflow restricts handling to konflux-internal-p02[bot], permitted title/version pattern and exactly the nudging file. It invokes shared insta-merge logic; this file alone does not establish additional CI or policy verdicts required before the nudge is emitted. The Operator Processor runs on an eligible bot push or manual dispatch.

nodes.title: G11 · Assemble + build RHOAI installer operator
lines: Processor: digests → operands map + source manifest metadata
Prefetch matching manifests; publish odh-rhel9-operator
Nightly/manual refresh is a separate route.
nodes.detail: The processor combines Build Config relatedImages with nudged digests, resolves image git.url/git.commit labels for manifest entries, and commits generated operands and prefetched content. A qualifying release-branch push builds the installer and nudges RHOAI Build Config bundle/bundle-patch.yaml. The nightly workflow is workflow_dispatch; its external cadence was not established.

nodes.title: G12 · Operator nudge → processed bundle / Helm
lines: Bot / file / title checks → bundle nudge merge
Process CSV + relatedImages / Helm values, then build
bundle-patch-only push is excluded from direct Tekton build.
nodes.detail: RHOAI Build Config bundle-insta-merge validates bot and changed-file feasibility. Process Operator Bundle handles the input change and commits processed bundle/Helm content. The generated content, not merely a bundle-patch edit, triggers the bundle build. Helm builds are parallel outputs; this diagram follows OLM bundle/catalog to the staged installation endpoint.

nodes.title: G13 · Bundle digest → catalog processing → FBC build
lines: catalog/catalog-patch.yaml nudge; process catalog content
Refresh PCC + select bundle snapshot; build FBC fragment
Policy / integration-test enforcement remains Q5.
nodes.detail: The bundle build nudges catalog/catalog-patch.yaml. Process FBC Fragment refreshes PCC, selects snapshot bundle images and commits catalog content. The direct FBC push trigger excludes catalog-patch-only changes. The inspected IntegrationTestScenario still names the 2.17 application and cannot establish the live 3.6 EC gate.

nodes.title: G14 · Promote selected FBC to stage ? Q5–Q6
lines: Push To Stage: workflow_dispatch; select FBC / latest nightly
Validate signed-image presence + catalog/PCC data
QE sign-off, release-policy binding and caller / cadence: OPEN
nodes.detail: Push To Stage accepts an FBC image (or LATEST_NIGHTLY), checks signed-image presence, validates/regenerates PCC, patches the stage catalog on Build Config main and monitors resulting catalog builds. A signature-presence check is not evidence of a full Enterprise Contract verdict. Required QE sign-off and the external trigger are not established.

nodes.title: QE-installable staged catalog
lines: Built stage catalog → OLM bundle → installer / module / workloads
nodes.detail: Endpoint requested by the user. Record the catalog digest, bundle digest, installer digest and related component digests together to trace which upstream commit is actually installable. Successful workflows alone do not prove the cluster installs the intended image set.

questions.title: Who moves ODH code into the Red Hat forks?
questions.text: Keep open: identify the exact source branch, target branch, bot/configuration, schedule, conflict owner, approvals, and backport rules for each component. Do stable → downstream main → rhoai-3.6 actually apply to both?

questions.title: Which TrustyAI tests actually block merges?
questions.text: Controller, module smoke and Prow tests are configured. Prow e2e is path-triggered. The classic branch-protection endpoint was inaccessible and the branch-rules endpoint returned no rules for upstream TrustyAI; confirm Tide/branch protection, required contexts, approvals and override policy. ODH main rules show one approval; this does not establish stable/incubation requirements.

questions.title: Are module and workload images intentionally built from different branches?
questions.text: EvalHub and TrustyAI workload builds target stable. The TrustyAI module build targets main, including the copy on stable. ODH installer manifests pin TrustyAI main. Confirm that this split is intentional and that a compatible module + workload + EvalHub set is tested together.

questions.title: What makes an image set eligible for installer selection?
questions.text: Digest pins and image-update PRs exist. Confirm which successful tests or policy verdicts gate a component digest nudge, who owns ODH Build Config updates, and what prevents mismatches between the selected image, module manifests, and provider ConfigMaps. The EvalHub ConfigMap sync workflow checks drift after main pushes and nightly; it does not itself promote changes.

questions.title: Which QE / Enterprise Contract verdicts are mandatory?
questions.text: The source defines scan tasks and Early Gate testing, but that alone does not prove merge or stage enforcement. The inspected release integration-test YAML still names a 2.17 application. Confirm live 3.6 IntegrationTestScenarios, release policy, required BVT/e2e suites, exceptions and whether Early Gate is required.

questions.title: Who triggers and approves promotion to the staged catalog?
questions.text: Push To Stage is workflow_dispatch and validates that a signed FBC image exists plus catalog/PCC data. Confirm the external caller or schedule, required QE sign-off, supported OCP versions and the exact catalog image/namespace QE installs. Next-development examples use rhoai-3.6; confirm when EA branches are the intended stream.

questions.title: Who authorizes SDK releases and consumer uptake?
questions.text: Confirm tag/release ownership, required PyPI environment reviewers and whether successful SDK CI must precede production publication. Identify owners for consumer dependency bump PRs and the supported SDK/service/sidecar compatibility set; the inspected workflows do not automate this handoff.

questions.text: Confirm the contrib release branch/channel, immutable digest, supported architectures and security/QE acceptance for each ODH/RHOAI release. Establish any downstream rebuild/mirror and relatedImages mapping instead of assuming it. Resolve overlapping RULER publishers and verify the manual all-images matrix covers the intended adapters.
